ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZiT7eA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDJHl8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 73, "title": "Correct ordered S-DSP dry and echo-send saturation before volume scaling", "body": "## Problem

`Dsp::sample` accumulates unrestricted dry and echo-send sums across all eight voices. The latest echo correction then narrows the master-scaled dry sum to signed 16 bits, allowing multi-voice overflow to reverse output polarity. This is the corrective target identified in `latest_assessment`, and a prerequisite for reliable stereo mixing and echo feedback.

At baseline `5b9c5acbaa3686247d125107ef8040f91efbf7aa`, three voice contributions of +16384 produce `mix=49152`. With MVOL=127 and no audible echo, current arithmetic returns **-16768**. The predecessor returned +32767; neither value establishes the correct ordered-accumulation result. Saturating the voice accumulator before master scaling produces **32511**.

Evidence: [unbounded voice accumulation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/5b9c5acbaa3686247d125107ef8040f91efbf7aa/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L245-L255), [feedback and master-volume consumers](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/5b9c5acbaa3686247d125107ef8040f91efbf7aa/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L276-L289), and [Issue #71’s explicitly bounded contract](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/5b9c5acbaa3686247d125107ef8040f91efbf7aa/docs/issue-71-validation.md#reconciled-contract-established-before-golden-vectors).

Existing echo tests use one bounded voice; the mixed BRR/noise test also stays below saturation. They do not establish ordered multi-voice overflow behavior. See [echo tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/5b9c5acbaa3686247d125107ef8040f91efbf7aa/crates/snes-core/src/dsp_echo_tests.rs#L161-L203) and [bounded mixed-source test](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/5b9c5acbaa3686247d125107ef8040f91efbf7aa/crates/snes-core/src/dsp_noise_tests.rs#L336-L377).

## Expected outcome

Implement sample-level signed saturation of the independent dry and EON-selected echo-send accumulators in hardware voice order, before their existing downstream consumers.

Reconcile the exact operation order against these specification references before finalizing expectations:

- [Anomie/jwdonal S-DSP documentation, revision 1212](https://gist.github.com/nyanpasu64/a0d916ce6924912a7116682bf778e9a0#file-apudsp_jwdonal-txt), **SOUND GENERATION** and **VOLUME CONTROL & ECHO**, for voice ordering, signed volume products and accumulation bounds.
- [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), DSP voice/master volume descriptions, plus [EON/EFB/EVOL and echo writeback](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm#snesapudspechoregisters), for routing and downstream arithmetic.

The precise implementation contract to reconcile is, independently for left and right:

```text
C16(x) = clamp(x, -32768, 32767)
SAR = arithmetic right shift, rounding toward negative infinity

D = 0; S = 0
for voice i = 0 through 7:
    A = (post_envelope_output[i] * signed8(VOL[i])) SAR 7
    D = C16(D + A)
    if EON bit i is set:
        S = C16(S + A)
```

`S` accumulates the selected contributions independently; it cannot be reconstructed from the clipped dry total. Master volume applies after dry accumulation. Echo feedback adds to the bounded send accumulator using the reconciled existing feedback rules, including even RAM writeback. Saturating after every voice addition is observably different from wrapping, retaining an unrestricted sum, or clamping only after the last voice.

Retain supported FIR, feedback and scaled-volume endpoint behavior from #71. Do not simply remove the new casts to restore predecessor output. If reference reconciliation exposes an unsupported earlier requirement, correct the contract and its expectations with explicit evidence.

## Context and reproduction

Use original held-noise fixtures already supported by the tests: NON-selected voices, noise rate 0, source -32768, direct GAIN=64. Each post-envelope output is -16384; voice volume -128 contributes +16384, while volume +64 contributes -8192. Exercise the public DSP sample path after key-on delay, rather than assigning accumulator results.

Independent arithmetic anchors:

| Voice contributions in ascending voice order | Ordered accumulator | PCM with MVOL=64 | Echo word with EON selecting all, EFB=0 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16384, 16384, 16384 | 32767 | 16383 | 32766 |
| 16384, 16384, 16384, -8192 | 24575 | 12287 | 24574 |
| 16384, -8192, 16384, 16384 | 32767 | 16383 | 32766 |

The last two rows have the same unrestricted sum. Their different results distinguish ordered saturation from a final clamp. Add equivalent negative-overflow/cancellation cases with realizable source and volume values.

For the second row, selecting only voices 0–2 for EON must send 32767 before even writeback, while the dry accumulator remains 24575. Selecting only voice 3 must send -8192. These controls distinguish independent EON accumulation from reuse of the dry result.

Scope is the accumulation correction, its consumer interactions, original numerical/integration tests, and updated validation/provenance records. No new DSP subcycle scheduler, IPL implementation, frontend feature, cartridge behavior or unrelated refactoring is required.

Planning inspected repository code, tests, guidance and history only. External reference contents and physical hardware were not inspected, and no emulator suites were rerun. The counterexample is static source arithmetic. Record any source ambiguity explicitly; research-emulator agreement alone is corroboration, not physical verification.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Document the reconciled voice order, product rounding, per-addition bounds, independent EON routing and downstream narrowing order, citing exact specification sections. Separate documented facts, derived vectors and any remaining convention. Implement the correction; a documentation-only audit does not close this Issue.
- [ ] Add original independent numerical tests through `Dsp::sample` for positive/negative overflow, overflow followed by cancellation, reordered contributions, early/late voice slots including voice 7, silence, and bounded inputs. Include the +49152/MVOL=127 reproduction and the table above. Expectations must come from documented arithmetic, not captured production output or production helpers.
- [ ] Cover asymmetric stereo volumes, signed volume endpoints and negative rounding; EON=0, all voices and selected subsets; and separate dry/send clipping. Verify exact PCM and little-endian echo bytes. Include nonzero feedback and audible echo composition, mute and echo-write-disable controls, retaining existing FIR/endpoint assertions.
- [ ] Add an original MIT SPC700 guest built from source and uploaded through the existing firmware-free protocol. The guest must configure multiple voices via `$F2/$F3`, exercise overflow and cancellation plus an EON selection change, and record observable register/echo-memory results. Assert independently derived steady-state PCM and RAM bytes with bounded acknowledgements/completion and no core error. Do not inject private voice/accumulator state or expected results. Record code/data provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Compare whole and irregular APU tick partitions for the new multi-voice scenario: every PCM sample, all DSP registers and relevant echo RAM must agree, with independent numerical checkpoints and unchanged cadence assertions.
- [ ] Demonstrate that focused overflow/cancellation regressions fail against the exact baseline and pass with the correction, using an isolated implementation-stage checkout. Record commands and actual results.
- [ ] Pass the following existing gates, plus executable commands for the new focused tests:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --lib dsp::echo_tests
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dsp_echo
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dsp_noise
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dsp_pitch
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dsp_envelope
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

Use the documented README compiler selection or test-port override when necessary. Build fixtures before browser execution. Preserve controller, DMA/HDMA and existing audio regressions; cleared-game source pins, hashes, replay lengths, gameplay/negative-control assertions and numerical music/effect checks must remain intact. Use only original or provenance-approved source-built fixtures; acquire no commercial ROMs or firmware.

- [ ] Update README and validation evidence with actual passes, failures and unperformed checks. Preserve all 24 supplied inventory scopes and statuses: 22 partial, `ppu-raster` and `pal` unimplemented, none verified. Remaining `dsp-voices` work includes independent BRR-filter 1–3 evidence, exhaustive interpolation phases and simultaneous key/mixing combinations. Live echo-register sampling, hidden envelopes, subcycle register/RAM interactions and physical startup/reset behavior remain separate work. Passing these tests establishes neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
